[2026-08-04 | AMZN | Overweight | -1.9% | -1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AMZN: build toward 1.0x standard weight in tranches, and only extend toward 1.15–1.25x after a confirmed breakout. Do not initiate at the 277.42 print — start with ~30–35% of target only if AMZN stabilizes around the 271.58 gap-day close, add ~30% only on a constructive retest of 262–266 that then reclaims 271.58 (or closes above 278.02), and reserve ~15–20% for a close above 287.20 that holds 2–3 sessions on >90M volume. The structural invalidation is a decisive daily close below 262.01 (the unfilled 239.82–262.01 gap): no adds there, cap or cut exposure, and do not average down. Size for the tail — cap risk at the 261.50 stop near 0.5% of portfolio equity and check that a gap-through toward 239.82 does not exceed ~1.0–1.25%; with ATR up 42.6% to 9.823 (~3.5% of spot), cut per-tranche share count ~30% versus pre-gap sizing. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: **The business argument is the decisive one, and the conservative seat concedes it.** Revenue accelerated to +19.6% y/y from +16.6%; operating income +43.2% to $27.5B on a 13.7% margin versus 11.4%; G&A −6% and stock comp −7.6% in absolute dollars while marketing barely moved — that is structural overhead leverage, not a one-quarter artifact. Q2 operating cash flow was a record $45.4B (+40%) and TTM OCF $161.4B (+33%), against $176B of cash and securities, ~$43.9B net cash, 21x interest coverage, 0.75x gross-debt-to-liquidity and only ~$3.3B due within twelve months. The conservative analyst's own words are that this "supports owning a core AMZN position," and the neutral analyst is right that adjusted EPS ~$2.16 with operating income +43.2% is "not a broken business." A franchise that just accelerated revenue at $200B quarterly scale while expanding margins 230bps does not support anything below Overweight — it argues only about the price at which you accumulate.

**The bear wins the entry point, and that is a sizing instruction, not a thesis.** Price sits 8.72% above the 10-EMA (255.16), 12.2% above the 50-SMA (247.19) and 17.7% above the 200-SMA (235.66) after a ~22% two-session move. The 08-04 candle was a −2.32% rejection from 287.20 that closed 0.22% back below the upper Bollinger band (278.02) after one day above it; volume decayed 129.05M → 90.83M → 69.75M (−46% from the peak); ATR repriced +42.6% in three sessions to 9.823. At 277.42 the immediate arithmetic is poor — roughly +3.5% to 287.20 versus −5.6% to the gap edge. And the aggressive analyst's "+21% upside" uses a measured move into the low 330s that requires a breakout not yet in evidence; from 271.58 the first real resistance is 5.7% away. Meanwhile the MACD line traveled from −3.75 to +4.809 in four sessions — a vertical spike that is confirmation of the move already made and is mean-revert-prone, not an early signal.

**Where I side against the conservative analyst: requiring the breakout before any capital forfeits the first leg.** His prescription — no position until stabilization above 271.58 or a confirmed close above 287.20 — is directionally prudent but treats a post-catalyst re-rating as untouchable. The lesson from this name is unambiguous: Underweight calls on AMZN on 07-22, 07-24, 07-27 and 07-28 were followed by five-day outcomes of −7.4% then +17.0%, +22.7% and +20.2%, and the 07-24 and 07-28 reflections both concluded that caution should have been expressed through sizing and post-event confirmation rather than a directional bearish stance. The 07-28 GOOGL reflection adds the matching cross-ticker lesson: do not defer all capital behind stacked triggers that can forfeit the first leg of a repair. I also note the conservative's "unverified catalyst" objection is partly answered by the neutral: a fresh 10-Q accepted around 07-31 exists; the gap still lacks a clean verified causal story (there is no news feed in the dataset), but absence of confirmation is not bearish confirmation.

**Where I side against the aggressive analyst: the 263 tranche math is broken and the "capped downside" is fiction.** The conservative and neutral analysts are both right that at 263 with a 261.50 stop the per-share risk is only ~1.50 — roughly 0.15 ATR — so scaling that tranche to the same fixed dollar risk as the 271.58 tranche would mechanically buy 6–7x the shares at the most fragile entry, right above invalidation. The original plan's fixed-dollar-risk instruction is therefore suspended for that rung: the retest tranche must be capped by notional exposure and portfolio weight, not by equal-risk arithmetic against a 1.5-point stop, and it requires a reclaim of 271.58 or a constructive close above 266–267 before execution. Likewise, the 261.50 stop is not a guaranteed fill — this stock gapped −9% on 2026-02-06 and −3.51% on 07-23 — so the position must be stress-tested against the 239.82 gap origin (~11–13% below spot), not just against the stop. The Bezos sale (~15M shares, under one session's volume of 69–129M) is not thesis-breaking, but the article's own note that AMZN dipped overnight on the headline makes it exactly the kind of supply signal that argues for stabilization-first entries rather than assuming the first touch is a gift.

**Fundamental risks are monitor-only, and I am naming the tripwires.** TTM free cash flow is −$11.6B on capex at 27% of revenue; debt is +93% to $132.2B in six months with net cash halved from $64.2B to $43.9B and interest expense +155%; D&A is +31.3% and rising as a share of revenue; contractual obligations run ~$650B with no buyback and a rising share count; and roughly 66% of Q2 pretax income came from private-stake revaluation marks, leaving adjusted EPS ~$2.16 versus $5.75 reported at ~35x adjusted TTM EPS. Those are real and they are why this is Overweight-sized staging rather than a Buy-everything call. The gates for downgrading toward Hold: capex growth failing to decelerate below revenue growth across two quarters, TTM FCF deteriorating further, net cash flipping to net debt, interest coverage compressing materially from 21x (versus 37x prior), and any reversal of the private-stake marks that produces an optical EPS decline. A reversal of the marks plus a capex-driven net-debt flip would justify stepping down to Hold/Underweight regardless of the tape.

**What would change the call upward or downward.** Upward toward Buy: a close above 287.20 holding 2–3 sessions on >90M volume with the 50-SMA turning up (it has only just stopped falling — 246.38 on 07-30 to 247.19), which is the trigger for the final tranche and permission to push toward 1.15–1.25x. Downward: a decisive daily close below 262.01 on volume invalidates the entire 239.82–262.01 gap structure; per the plan and both analysts, stop adding entirely, reassess, and do not average down — the statistical target of a failed gap is the 239.82 origin, with 255.16 and the 247.19–247.42 shelf as interim references.

**Stated evidence gaps I am not underwriting:** the catalyst behind the 07-30/07-31 volume explosion cannot be verified from the supplied material; whether 287.20 is an all-time high is unknown because the dataset begins 2026-01-02; the AWS "60.3% of operating income" figure is an unaudited single-author claim; the options-implied upside, sector-rotation and milestone-flow arguments are backward-looking or unverified secondary reporting; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context was supplied, so all sizing is expressed as multiples of a standard AMZN allocation and as fixed fractions of portfolio equity for the caller to apply to their own book.

**Price Target**: 305.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
Five-day alpha of −1.8% (raw −1.9%) means the Overweight call lost money out of the gate, though at five days against a 3–6 month horizon this is far too short to judge the thesis itself — the call's own gates (reclaim of 271.58, close above 287.20) were never triggered, so the small loss reflects price drift rather than falsification. What the window does support is the bear's entry-point clause: refusing to initiate at 277.42 and demanding stabilization at 271.58 was correct, and the retest/cap-on-notional discipline on the 262–266 tranche kept a −1.9% move from becoming a real drawdown. What it undercuts is my pushback against the conservative analyst — the "don't forfeit the first leg" argument bought nothing here, since the first leg went down. Next time, express directional conviction only at or below the stabilization level I already identified, and treat the gap between current spot and that entry as unearned optimism rather than as upside the call should have owned.

[2026-08-03 | AMZN | Overweight | -2.1% | -4.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AMZN, built in tranches rather than taken at the 284.02 print: I am adopting the neutral analyst's calibration over both the plan's 40% starter and the conservative 10–15% token. Take a 20–25% starter of one standard AMZN allocation with limit orders in 278.00 down to 273.23 (the unfilled 273.23–278.29 gap floor), no chase above 287, and treat 250 on a daily *close* as full structural invalidation of the core tranche — which, per the conservative's catch, means the 246–250 shelf add is a separate trade with its own invalidation below the rising 200-SMA (~235.35) or a confirmed close back above 250, not an add into a violated stop. Reserve ~20% for a volume-confirmed break and retest above 287.20, ~15% for a flush holding ~265, and cap total exposure at 60% until the AWS segment disclosure, the missing 119/139 news records, and the $92B AFS-tag reconciliation are in hand, then 70%. Horizon 6–12 months; the ~10% per-share risk on the starter puts roughly 2.0–2.5% of the full allocation at risk, which is the right size for a 3.5%-ATR, two-gap tape.

**Investment Thesis**: **The direction is not close — the operating engine is accelerating, and the aggressive analyst won that argument unrefuted.** Q2 revenue ~$200.6B at +19.6% y/y is *faster* than Q1's +16.6% (that is reacceleration at scale, not decay); Q2 operating income $27.5B at +43.2% with margin expanding to 13.7% from 11.4%; H1 operating cash flow $71.4B at +44.2%. The decisive detail is that this margin expansion happened *while* D&A rose 32% and marketing grew only 3.9% with G&A down 3.9% — the depreciation wave from the AI buildout is already in the P&L and the business is outrunning it, which is the definition of operating leverage rather than accounting fluff. Stripping the mark-up still leaves clean Q2 EPS ~$1.97 vs ~$1.54 (+28%). Against $176.1B of cash and securities, ~$30B net cash, ~25% debt/equity and ~21x interest coverage, negative TTM FCF of −$11.6B is a *funding choice* on a net-cash balance sheet, not a solvency event — and $27.5B of quarterly operating income swamps $1.314B of quarterly interest even after the +155% y/y rise. The conservative analyst conceded all of this ("not accounting fluff"), which is why the floor on the rating is Overweight and not Hold.

**Where the bear/skeptic side won, and where I overrule the trader's plan.** First, the conservative analyst scored a real, decisive point that the plan does not survive as written: it simultaneously reserves 30% to *buy* the 246–250 confluence shelf and declares a daily close below 250 an exit for the whole position. If price closes under 250, the stop has fired; you cannot then buy the same level with the same stop. That is exactly how a "reserve" turns into averaging down through the 239.82–265.00 gap. Second, the neutral analyst is right that a daily-close stop bounds *intended* risk, not *realized* risk: with ATR at 9.95 (3.5% of price) and two unfilled gaps beneath, a gap through 250 fills lower, so the plan's modeled ~4% full-allocation risk on a 40% starter is optimistic. Third, the conservative rightly flags that the sizing sequence is backwards — the plan says "cap at 70% until the data gaps close" and then front-loads 40% *before* those gaps close, when the missing input (AWS segment revenue, margin and backlog) is precisely the demand side of a capex program running at ~27% of revenue. Note also the factual correction I accept: the $650B of contractual obligations are Amazon's *own commitments to pay* ($78.1B due within twelve months, plus ~$132B long-term debt and $104.9B of leases), not a customer backlog — the bull's "contracted forward demand" framing converts a documented liability into an undocumented asset. And at 284 the headline ~12x multiple is an artifact: clean annualized EPS puts AMZN near ~35x, and 68% of H1 net income is non-operating with $122.3B of non-marketable equity on the book (from $16.2B). Using the mark-up to call the stock cheap would be an error I am not making.

**Where the conservative analyst overreached, and why the answer is not 10–15%.** A token starter that barely moves the outcome is not risk management; it is a decision to underperform a re-rating on purpose. The record is explicit about this. AMZN Underweights on 2026-07-23, 07-24 and 07-27 produced +0.8%, +17.0% and +22.7% raw returns against SPY inside five days — the persistent lesson is that being structurally defensive into an accelerating franchise has repeatedly cost more alpha than the tape caution saved. The 2026-07-21 Overweight was the mirror-image error in the other direction (−6.7% raw, −5.8% alpha) because a starter was taken *ahead of* every stated confirmation gate into a decaying tape. The synthesis of those two lessons is exactly the neutral's structure: participate now, at a gap-floor limit rather than the print, but at a size that survives a gap through the stop and with the additive tranches strictly confirmation-gated. That is 20–25% here, not 10–15% and not 40%.

**Sequencing and risk architecture I am adopting.** (1) Starter 20–25% of a standard allocation, limits 278.00 → 273.23, no market order at 284.02 (13.5% above both the 10-EMA 250.22 and VWMA 250.17, ~4% above the upper Bollinger at 272.99). (2) ~20% on a break above 287.20 on above-average volume *with* a successful retest of 278 — not on the poke alone, and not while the 10-EMA (rising ~7–8 points/session from ~250) is still far below price. (3) ~15% on a flush that holds ~265 (upper edge of the 239.82–265.00 gap), or on a confirmed close back above 250 if the shelf is tested first. (4) The 246–250 confluence shelf add (10-EMA 250.22 / VWMA 250.17 / 50-SMA ~246.38) is a *separate* position with invalidation below the rising 200-SMA at ~235.35 and size recalculated against that wider risk — I am explicitly rejecting the plan's contradictory version of it. Core-tranche invalidation is a daily close below ~250, on a closing basis only (tight stops in a 3.5%-ATR tape get harvested); on a gap through it, accept that the stop under-delivered and do not average in. Trail under the 10-EMA once price has held above 287 for several sessions. Total exposure 60% until the data gaps close, 70% after; no leverage and no options overlay on this name while AWS segment data is absent.

**What would change the call.** Down to Hold and a trim of Tranche 1 on any one of: a daily close below 250; capex/revenue materially above 27.0% with still no AWS segment disclosure to justify it; TTM FCF deteriorating beyond the H1 −$27.0B trajectory; further large debt issuance pushing annualized interest expense well past the ~$5.3B run-rate; or any markdown/writedown or delayed validation on the $122.3B non-marketable equity book. Up to Buy on: a positive TTM free cash flow print or capex/revenue rolling below ~25%; AWS segment revenue growth and margin disclosed and accelerating (the extract contains none of this); a real transaction validating the private-stake marks; plus a healthy 273–287 base with no distribution. Explicit evidence I am not underwriting and that should be requested before sizing past the starter: (i) no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog — the single biggest missing input for a 27%-of-revenue capex program; (ii) 119 of 139 news records missing, including the entire 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-01 window; (iii) a reported $92B AFS tag against a $97.9B portfolio showing only ~$7M of gross gains. My $315 target is a rough 6–12-month structural estimate, not a valuation-model output — no P/E, EV/EBITDA, or Q3 consensus data was supplied, and sizing is expressed only as fractions of a standard AMZN allocation because no holdings or cash context was provided.

**Price Target**: 315.0

**Time Horizon**: 6-12 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -4.1% (raw -2.1%) went against the Overweight call, but five days is far too short to test a 6–12 month operating-leverage thesis. What the window does undercut is the tactical layer: the 278.00–273.23 gap-floor limits did not cushion the entry, and the extension flags I logged (13.5% above the 10-EMA, ~4% above the upper Bollinger, ~35x clean EPS) proved to be the operative risk rather than the reacceleration story. Lesson for next time: when price is that stretched above its 10-EMA and sitting on unfilled gaps, treat the starter as unearned until a 273–287 base actually forms, rather than pre-positioning limits that assume the gap floor holds.

TTM D&A of ~$70.4B against a ~$151.0B TTM capex run-rate means depreciation is running at less than half of capex; Q1 2026 capex of $44.2B (+76.7% y/y) enters the depreciation schedule only when placed in service, quarters from now.
